tool_input.body:
Confirmed and fixed in `73855d5`. Verified against the source before acting: `LoadLayer` → `loadArchetype` uses `os.ReadFile` with its own `os.IsNotExist` split, so a permission error on the repo-local file returns immediately and never falls through to global — exactly as you described. `archetypeAttemptedPath`'s bare `err == nil` could not tell "absent" from "present but EACCES," so it reported global on any `Stat` failure.

Now a three-way split: `nil` → repo-local; `IsNotExist` → global, as before; anything else → repo-local, tagged `(unreadable)` so the operator's next step reads as `chmod` rather than "create this file."

**Small finding, and worth more than its size, because it is this cluster's signature defect for the third time.** That helper exists *specifically* to make the archetype failure actionable — it was added so `ethos-e05k`'s FAIL could name which layer is stale. Misreporting the layer produces a detail the operator cannot act on, which is `ethos-jw1z`'s own defect class. So within one file: the check swallowed load errors into a green PASS (`e05k`'s mode), the archetype name list was hardcoded and would silently stop monitoring a third archetype (`e05k` again), and the remediation path pointed at the wrong file (`jw1z`).

One shape underneath all three, now written into the fix's comment: **a fallback branch treating "I could not determine X" as "X is the default" is the same mistake as a check treating "I could not verify" as "verified."** That is the entire subject of this PR, reappearing inside the code written to eliminate it.

**One process note worth recording.** The regression test — which chmods the repo-local archetypes directory to `0o000`, skipped on Windows and as root — passed against the *buggy* code on its first draft. The assertion looked for `"global)"`; the real format is `"(global, path)"` with a comma. It was caught only because the protocol here requires running every new test against pre-fix code before trusting it. A test that passes before the fix is not coverage, and reading it would not have revealed that. Re-falsified with corrected assertions: fails pre-fix with `implement (global, .../001/...)` while the underlying error names the `002` repo-local tempdir, passes post-fix.

Gates: `make check` green with race, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exit 0, detached-env gate 28 ok / 0 FAIL.

tool_input.prompt:
A 13-finding review batch landed on PR #515 in <repo>, branch `fix/doctor-health-checks` (HEAD `73855d5`, clean, pushed, all six CI checks green including Bugbot). Do NOT create or switch branches or worktrees.

**Read the findings yourself** — there are too many to relay faithfully:

```
gh api graphql -f query='{ repository(owner: "punt-labs", name: "ethos") { pullRequest(number: 515) { reviewThreads(first: 50) { nodes { isResolved comments(first:1){nodes{databaseId path line author{login} body}} } } } } }' --jq '.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[] | select(.isResolved==false) | {cid: .comments.nodes[0].databaseId, who: .comments.nodes[0].author.login, path: .comments.nodes[0].path, line: .comments.nodes[0].line, body: .comments.nodes[0].body}'
```

Two from Copilot, eleven from qodo. **Verify each against the source before fixing it.** Some will be wrong — one already is, see below.

**ONE FINDING IS MISATTRIBUTED — do not "fix" it.** qodo's *"Some non-windows builds no longer compile"* (`procgroup_unix.go:1`) blames this branch for a pre-existing limitation. I checked: `GOOS=js` and `GOOS=plan9` fail in **`internal/process`**, not in your files — that package already excludes those platforms and has since long before this branch. Every shipped target builds clean: darwin/arm64, darwin/amd64, linux/arm64, windows/amd64, all exit 0. Reply on that thread explaining the misattribution with the evidence; change nothing. If you find I am wrong about that, say so with evidence and I will take it.

**Two I verified as real, both worth prioritising:**

**A — `CheckDelegatedWorkerArchetypes` silently drops the global layer when `os.UserHomeDir()` fails** (`archetype_check.go:97`, flagged by both reviewers). `globalRoot` stays `""` and the check quietly inspects one layer instead of two, then reports PASS or a partial FAIL as though it had looked at everything.

**This is the fourth time this cluster has reproduced the bug it was written to close, and the third time in this one file.** The shape, now stated in the code from the last fix: *a fallback treating "I could not determine X" as "X is the default" is the same mistake as a check treating "I could not verify" as "verified."* Here it is "I could not determine the global root" → "skip that layer silently" → green. `ethos doctor` is operator-facing diagnostics; it must fail loudly when it cannot determine a root it is supposed to inspect.

**B — `reapProcessGroup` returns `syscall.Kill`'s error raw** (`procgroup_unix.go:34`). `ESRCH` is the *expected* result when the group already exited — which is the common case, since you call it unconditionally after `Run()` returns. Treating "nothing left to reap" as a failure surfaces a confusing sandbox error. Swallow `ESRCH` specifically; keep every other errno.

**On the rest** — several qodo titles claim false-PASS behaviour ("Broken hooks can pass the health check", "Malformed hook calls pass as valid", "Inactive windows hooks pass doctor", "Doctor clears an uninspectable install", "Dormant repos hide active seal hooks"). Those are exactly this PR's subject matter, so treat them as high-prior-probability but still verify each; a false PASS claimed by a reviewer is not automatically a false PASS in the code. Two are documentation claims (`DESIGN.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`) asserting the docs misstate what the code does — on this branch a doc that overstates what it closes is a defect, so fix the prose to match reality rather than arguing scope.

**Standards, unchanged:**
- Every behavioural change needs a regression test **confirmed failing against pre-fix code**, with the pre-fix output pasted. Last round your own first-draft assertion passed against buggy code because it matched the wrong string format — you caught it by following this protocol. Keep doing that.
- `make check` green with race before every commit. No suppressions.
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exit 0, and spot-check darwin since you are touching build-tagged files.
- Detached gate; report both `ok` and `FAIL` counts.
- Commit incrementally. **Do not push; I push.**
- Update DES-077 and CHANGELOG for anything user-visible.

**Report in two parts: which findings you fixed, and which you rejected with the evidence.** I expect rejections in a batch this size, and a reviewer being wrong is a finding too. State what your fixes make worse; if "nothing," say what you checked.
